**Scanpath Studio** shows how people read. It draws eye-tracking-while-reading data over the text, where it sat on the screen, replays each reading, compares readers, and exports figures for a paper. This is a **beta**: the app, the Python API and the CLI may still change during 0.x.

**Get it**
- **Desktop app**, for your own data: the Windows, macOS and Linux downloads under *Assets* below.
- **With pip** (Python 3.11–3.14): `pip install -U scanpath-studio`, then `scanpath-studio`.
- **In the browser:** the [hosted demo](https://scanpath-studio.streamlit.app), on the bundled data.

[Documentation](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/) · [Ask a question](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/discussions/categories/q-a) · [Report a bug](https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio/issues/new?template=bug_report.md) · [Cite](https://lacclab.github.io/scanpath-studio/cite/)

**Held back in this beta:** the reading measures and summaries the app would compute from fixations. Corpus Analysis shows the measures your dataset brings, and the computations reference lists what each figure derives.
